segments.text: Your gut makes a hormone after every meal. It lasts about two minutes. Then your body destroys it.
It's called G L P one. A tiny peptide that tells the pancreas to release insulin when sugar is high, and quietly turns down hunger in the brain.
For decades, that two-minute lifespan made it useless as a drug. Medicine needed the same message — but a structure that could survive.
Enter Omnigent, from Databricks. A meta-harness for A I agents. One Y A M L agent. Tools, policies, and a live shareable session.
We define Protein Lab. Swap one line to change the model harness. The tools stay the same: Boltz for structure, render for stills, movie for the spin.
The agent calls Boltz in the cloud. Sequence in. Three D coordinates and confidence out. G L P one, folded live.
This is the fold family behind the biggest metabolic drugs of the decade. Natural G L P one dies in minutes. Engineered cousins last days — same idea, redesigned structure.
In the Omnigent UI, tool cards stream as they run. Policies guard the session. Share lets a teammate watch the science unfold in real time.
Sequence. Structure. Story. From gut hormone to drug design — orchestrated by Omnigent on Databricks. Try it: omni run, agents, protein lab.
